problem: End-to-end imitation-learning vision-only navigation models (ViNT, NoMaD, FlowNav) need large training data, are hard to interpret or certify, and tend to overfit to the recorded expert trajectory, reacting poorly to unseen obstacles.
motivation: Real-world autonomous systems need interpretable, certifiable and modularly improvable navigation. Advances in MPC, traversability segmentation, visual place recognition and pose estimation make it possible to build a hybrid vision-only system in which a model-based controller produces the final actions.
key_idea: A hierarchical system that localizes on a topological image graph with VPR, picks a subgoal pixel on the traversable mask using relative-yaw estimation, and drives an MPPI controller with a cost defined in pixel space plus IPM-based collision avoidance.
insight: Modular components let failures be traced to specific parts (traversability errors on white walls, imprecise IPM, no temporal context). Compared with ViNT/NoMaD, which overfit to the expert path, PixelNav reacts more explicitly to unseen obstacles and reaches the goal more often (GRR 0.9/0.8 vs. at best 0.7/0.0). The cost is more indirect collisions and freezes, since there is no memory of obstacles that have left the field of view.
method: Topological graph construction: DPVO scale-free visual odometry gives 2D poses. Nodes are images. Edges are added when a Euclidean criterion (distance < rho*mu) and an angular criterion (heading difference < phi_max) both hold, to keep transitions feasible for a unicycle robot.
VPR localization and planning: AnyLoc (DINOv2 features, GeM pooling) finds the closest node, Dijkstra/A* finds the path to the goal node, and a node at an offset along the path is the subgoal image.
Traversability estimation: a SegFormer binary segmentation model, trained on a subset of the EgoWalk dataset (SAM-based auto-labels), gives the traversable mask T_t.

Subgoal pixel selection: SuperPoint + SuperGlue matches, RANSAC essential matrix and yaw extraction give the relative angle alpha. A ray at alpha is traced through the traversable mask, and the pixel at about 2/3 of the segment is chosen (fallback: the closest mask pixel).

MPPI low-level controller: a unicycle model with (v, w) controls. The subgoal cost is the pixel-space distance between the projected robot state and the subgoal pixel. The collision cost counts mask-contour points, back-projected to the ground by IPM, that lie within r_safe of the robot. A control-effort penalty is added.
Deployment: ROS 2 with separate nodes, TensorRT for the segmentation and SuperPoint/SuperGlue models, on an AgileX Tracer robot with an Azure Kinect RGB camera (depth unused).

setting.backbone: Modular: SegFormer (trained traversability), DINOv2/AnyLoc (frozen VPR), SuperPoint+SuperGlue (pretrained), DPVO, and an MPPI controller
setting.training_data: SegFormer trained on a subset of the EgoWalk traversability dataset (SAM auto-labeled); other components are pretrained and used off the shelf; no end-to-end navigation training
setting.observation: monocular RGB (known intrinsics, fixed camera height)
setting.action_space: continuous unicycle velocities (linear, angular) from MPPI
setting.privileged: none at test time; a prior expert traversal is recorded to build the topological graph

numbers_note: Only real-world custom metrics (ADC, AIC, TDCR, AF, GRR) on two indoor spaces; no canonical benchmark results. For reference, PixelNav Space #1: ADC 0.7, AIC 0.7, TDCR 0.3, AF 0.0, GRR 0.9; Space #2: ADC 0.7, AIC 1.1, TDCR 0.2, AF 0.8, GRR 0.8.
results: In two real indoor spaces with 9 runs each per method, PixelNav reaches the goal at 0.9 (Space 1) and 0.8 (Space 2), versus NoMaD 0.7/0.0 and ViNT 0.2/0.0. It has lower target-obstacle collision rates (0.3/0.2 vs. 0.5 for NoMaD) but higher indirect collisions and some freezes in Space 2.
limitations: Small-scale evaluation (two spaces, 3 trials per condition) with manual interventions, and no standard benchmark.
No temporal memory, which causes many indirect collisions and failures at corners. Traversability errors on white textureless walls and imprecise IPM (which needs a large r_safe) also hurt.
Assumes a fixed known camera height, known intrinsics and a camera orthogonal to the ground; freezes occur when there is no traversable area.
